rename.from: JUnit5RunnerListener doesn't add dynamic containers to test plan
rename.to: JUnitPlatformTestTree does not add dynamic containers to test plan

body:
Thanks for raising the issue.

Your analysis is correct: it is not currently possible to add a dynamic `TestDescriptor` for a _container_. 

Your example engine is based on an older version of the code base. `JUnit5RunnerListener` is now `JUnitPlatformRunnerListener`.

In any case, the actual problem is in `JUnitPlatformTestTree.addDynamicDescription()`, and I will soon be committing a fix for that.

FYI: I think you may be slightly confused about `request.getRootTestDescriptor()`.

That will return the `EngineDescriptor` returned from `discover()`. That's why I tracked your custom `RootTestDescriptor` separately in my updated version of your engine.
Also, you created your _container_ as a `TestTestDescriptor` when it should in fact be a `ContainerTestDescriptor`.

I was just observing that about the rootTestDescriptor. Thank you. I'm still learning as I go. :smile: 

The `TestTestDescriptor` for my container was probably from me just experimenting with it to see if returning different values for `isTest` and `isContainer` made any difference (which I didn't suspect it would and it didn't but I thought it worth a try). I must have forgotten to change it back.

Thank you for getting this updated to get me going again. I'll watch for the fix. Thank you again!
FYI: this has been resolved in `master` in 47d20a7448d441f3239b9b2ace53fe45396d9859.

issue.title: Allow TestEngines to be completely dynamic

repository.name: junit-framework
repository.description: ✅ The programmer-friendly testing framework for Java and the JVM

issue.body:
## Status Quo

It is currently impossible to create a custom `TestEngine` that is completely dynamic in nature.

The reason is that a completely dynamic engine will not have any statically registered children and will therefore get summarily _pruned_ by `org.junit.platform.launcher.core.Root.pruneEmptyTestEngines()`.
## Deliverables
- [x] Allow test engines to be completely dynamic (i.e., don't prune engines without children).
